title: Tools like Rive and Phase are making Designers' lives easier by bringing more motion and fluidity to our projects
description: Why animation matters in product design and when to use Phase (quick transitions from Figma) or Rive (real-time interactions).
updateNote: Update note (2026): some of the tools mentioned have changed or been replaced since publication. Focus on the principle behind each one, not the name.

related.title: Servientrega
related.body: In practice: a complex journey turned into a simple visual experience.

blocks.text: A big challenge in product design is turning static, monotonous interfaces into dynamic, engaging experiences. Luckily, tools like Rive and Phase are making that easier than ever, bringing amazing animations to our prototypes and digital products.

These platforms are extremely intuitive, especially if you already work with Figma or Framer. Let's explore how these tools work, what makes them so powerful and which one might be the best choice for your project.
Why are animations essential in design?
Animations aren't just a “special touch” in design. They help to:

items.title: Guide
items.body: Shows what happens after the interaction.

blocks.caption: The three roles of motion mentioned in the article.

items: Guide users: Showing what happens after an interaction.
Make interfaces more intuitive: Microinteractions create a sense of immediate response.
Engage users: A well-planned animated experience can increase engagement time.

blocks.text: But to create efficient animations that are integrated into the product, we need tools that combine ease and power. That's exactly what Rive and Phase offer.
Phase: Quick, simple animations for product designers
Phase is ideal if you're already used to tools like Figma. It was built for product designers who need to create animated prototypes intuitively and without hassle.

items: Familiar, intuitive interface: It feels like you're working in Figma itself.
Figma integration: Export your designs easily and start animating directly in Phase.
Handy timeline: Full control over timing and transitions.
Export to multiple formats: Great for sharing GIFs or videos with teams and stakeholders.

blocks.text: I used Phase on a redesign project for a SaaS platform. With it, I created animated transitions between screens in under 2 hours. The client loved the smooth animations, and the development team integrated the transitions as JSON with no rework.

data.title: Transitions between screens
data.body: In Phase, the transition links one screen to the next: the tapped element turns into the next screen.

blocks.text: Rive: Take your animation to a new level with interactivity
Rive goes beyond basic animations. It lets you create dynamic interactions that react to user behavior, ideal for apps, games or digital products that need real-time responses.

items: Advanced editor: Features like rigging and path animations for maximum control.
Real-time interactivity: Create animations that respond to user clicks, taps or gestures.
Runtime export: Integrates directly into frameworks like Flutter and Unity.
Optimized performance: Animations are lightweight, perfect for web and mobile.

blocks.text: I created an interactive character animation in Rive for a kids' education app. The character reacted to touch and guided the user through the app. The solution increased engagement by 25%, according to interaction metrics.

data.title: A character that reacts to touch
data.body: In Rive, the animation works like a state machine: idle, cursor nearby and tap. Hover and click.

blocks.text: Conclusion: motion and fluidity at your fingertips
Tools like Rive and Phase are revolutionizing the way we create animated prototypes and dynamic interactions. Choosing the best one depends on the type of project:

items: Need quick animations integrated with Figma? Go with Phase.
Want to create advanced interactions for apps and games? Choose Rive.
